sections.title: Habit and leaves
sections.text: Common sorrel is a perennial native across Europe and Asia, forming a rosette of arrow-shaped leaves with two basal lobes. Its erect, branched stems reach about 30–100 cm; basal leaf blades are about 3.5–12 cm long.

sections.title: Flowers and seeds
sections.text: The species is dioecious, with male and female flowers on separate plants. Small reddish flowers form a leafless panicle; the fruits are triangular achenes enclosed by membranous valves. The plate matches these leaves, flowering stems and fruits.

sections.title: Edibility and oxalic acid
sections.text: Young, sour leaves are eaten as a vegetable or seasoning. They contain oxalic acid, so large or repeated portions are inadvisable, particularly for people prone to kidney stones or advised to limit oxalates.
